key_insight: Dynamic routing gives LLMs a second test-time adaptation axis beyond chain-of-thought, and simple confidence-based selection can improve performance without any gradient updates.
engineering_relevance: For computational engineering workflows, this suggests a lightweight way to boost model robustness and efficiency at inference time by choosing among layer-routing programs instead of retraining.
method: Test a handful of candidate routing programs using 3 or 10 demonstrations.
Select programs by how well they predict demo labels, then arbitrate with the model’s own confidence.
Combine routing with chain-of-thought when beneficial, since the two help on different queries.
evidence_signal: Across 49 MMLU tasks and seven post-trained models, confidence-based routing improved results on average, and on ARC-AGI a 7B model’s accuracy roughly doubled when using routing.
watch_item: Routing gains can be fragile if a poor route pushes the residual stream out of the distribution expected by later layers, so selection and stability checks matter.
paper_title: Dynamic Routing as a New Dimension for Test-time Versatility of LLMs
